cells.tense: You stand in the clearing, and what is left is fairly shared out.
cells.act: keep what the change produced from drifting
cells.ask: Name one good thing that came through a recent ending. Do the small upkeep it needs this week, before it slips. Just that one.
cells.core:
You're standing in a clearing, and the change has already happened. What's left over — the time, the people, the things that were shared — is getting divided fairly, and it's happening without much arguing about it. You give what you said you'd give. What comes back to you comes back. The ending did its work, and what it produced is being held steady by the exchange it lives in.

Because the clearing is real, the next thing is to keep what it produced from drifting. Pick one good thing that came through a recent ending. Something you still have. Do the small upkeep it needs in the next week, before you decide whether it's worth keeping long-term. That's how the fair exchange stays alive. It doesn't take much. Just the one thing, and the upkeep it actually needs.
cells.sheetLine: What the ending left is being shared fairly now.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange as things end and clear
cells.place: The clearing where what was must finish so what will can begin

cells.tense: You're braced for the clearing to tip before you're done giving.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: In an ending you're in, do your part these next days, the whole of it, and leave the rest alone. No checking what others carry.
cells.core:
You're in a clearing, and some part of you is bracing. The exchange has gotten watchful, like you're keeping a hand on the scale the whole time so the ending doesn't tip against you. You count what you're owed before you hand anything over. You keep a running total of who has given what here. Fairness done that hard starts to slow the clearing itself, because nobody can move while the accounting is running.

So carry your own part these next days. The whole of it, at the pace you can manage, without checking what anyone else is holding. Leave their part where it is, even if it's going slowly. You may find that the fairness you were protecting was mostly yours to carry in the first place, and the clearing moves better when you're not holding the whole ledger.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding the scale while the clearing waits.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange as things end and clear
cells.place: The clearing where what was must finish so what will can begin

cells.tense: You're still at the door of an ending that already closed.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Take something you're still owed from an ending that's over. Look once, put on paper what it actually was and whether it can still be paid. Then leave it.
cells.core:
There's an ending behind you that you haven't quite come through. You're at the door, still, and the exchange around it went one way. People have moved on from the clearing. You're still accounting for something that left the room. The fairness is clear inside you; it just isn't moving between anyone anymore.

Look closely at a single debt from that ending. Not the whole of it — one piece. Put on paper what it actually was: not what it took, not what it meant, just the thing itself and whether it can still be paid. Then leave it where it is. You're not required to make peace with it. You're sorting what's still real from what's already over, and that distinction does more than anything you could ask for.
cells.sheetLine: You're at a door that already closed.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange as things end and clear
cells.place: The clearing where what was must finish so what will can begin

cells.tense: You're already balancing the clearing, and you'd say it just worked out.
cells.act: weigh what you know before it leaves you
cells.ask: Next time a room is settling something, notice what you see about what's fair before you speak. Weigh it a beat, then act if you still want to.
cells.core:
In this clearing, someone is quietly evening things out. Taking less so another person can have their share. Saying the right word when an ending starts to go badly. Asked about it, you'd say the group just found its way through. You wouldn't call it yours. The fairness is real and it's yours, and the way you talk about it makes it sound like something that happened to the room.

Slow down by one beat. The next time you're in a room where something is being settled, let yourself know what you see about what's fair before you say or do anything. Don't announce it. Don't make it a principle. Just weigh it long enough to feel it as yours, then act or don't act, whichever is right. Knowing your hand is in the balancing doesn't change what you do. It does change who gets credit for it, even if the only person who ever finds out is you.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness is yours. The room gets the credit.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange as things end and clear
cells.place: The clearing where what was must finish so what will can begin
